text: Hi! It looks like you're trying to build a droid council.
I'm Clippy. Here's what happened when forty-six droids tried to do one job.
One task. A six-file Python package, each file with its own tests.
Run A, one droid. Run B, a council of forty-six.
The council splits the task into thirteen leaves, then runs a fixed worker pool over them.
No droid ever spawns a droid. The orchestrator owns every node. That's the trick.
Now watch the clock. For the first one hundred and sixty-six seconds, the council builds nothing.
It's opening sessions. The lone droid has been writing code since second six.
But look at the execute phase. Thirteen workers. Thirteen hundred and forty-nine seconds of work, inside one hundred and thirty seconds of clock.
Ten point four times the throughput.
So who wins end to end? The single droid. Two hundred and sixty-one seconds against three hundred and ninety-one.
And ten thousand credits against eighty-two thousand.
A council pays off when the work is bigger than one context window.
Below that, you're just paying for session startup.
